issues.description: Method name mismatch: The exercise requires a public method named singFarmSong() on class Farm. The problem statement (and the template) reference and declare singFarmSong(), but the solution implements a public method named playFarmSong() instead. This naming inconsistency will confuse students about which method to implement and will break automated checks/tests that expect Farm.singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's public API match the specification: rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to playFarmSong(). Ensure the solution provides a public void singFarmSong() so it matches the problem statement and template.

issues.description: Concept: the Farm class method that plays/sings the Old MacDonald song. Problem statement and template define and refer to a method named singFarmSong(). Template: declares public void singFarmSong() (stub). Solution: implements the same functionality under the method named playFarmSong(). Students reading the exercise will expect to implement or call singFarmSong(), but the provided solution's public API uses playFarmSong(), creating a direct identifier mismatch that can block mapping requirements to the implementation and break tests or example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution API match the problem statement and template: rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method in the solution that delegates to playFarmSong() (e.g., public void singFarmSong() { playFarmSong(); }). Ensure the method signature and visibility exactly match the template/problem (public void singFarmSong()).
